pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 🌐 **Strand 3 — Communication Networks**
Sub-strand 2: Internet and Social Media

Social media can connect, teach and empower, or harm, deceive and distract. In this unit you will weigh the advantages against the risks and learn how to avoid the dangers. You will also master reply, reply all and forward in email.

pages.title: Content standard and lessons
pages.body:
> 🎯 **Content standard**
- **B9.3.2.1** Demonstrate the use of social networking and electronic mail.

> 🧭 **What you will be able to do**
- **B9.3.2.1.1** Identify the advantages and risks in the use of social media platforms.

> 🗺️ **Lessons in this unit**
- 9.1 Benefits and Risks of Social Media; Reply, Reply All and Forward

**Core competencies developed:** Digital Literacy (DL5.1).

pages.title: Benefits and Risks of Social Media; Reply, Reply All and Forward
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B9.3.2.1.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- illustrate the benefits of social media;
- discuss the risks and how to avoid them;
- explore reply, reply all and forward in email.
| **Benefits of social media** | **Illustration** |
|---|---|
| Communication and staying connected | Video-calling relatives abroad |
| Learning and information | Educational YouTube channels; following NaCCA, GES and WAEC pages |
| Business and jobs | Selling products on WhatsApp Business and Instagram; job adverts on LinkedIn |
| Creativity and self-expression | Sharing art, music, poetry and coding projects |
| Community action | Organising clean-ups, blood donation drives and fundraising |
| Emergency information | Weather and safety alerts shared quickly |
| **Risk** | **How to avoid it** |
|---|---|
| Cyberbullying and harassment | Block and report bullies; don’t reply in anger; keep evidence; tell a trusted adult |
| Privacy loss and identity theft | Use private account settings; don’t share personal details, location or ID numbers |
| Scams and phishing | Never click suspicious links or share OTPs; verify offers through official channels |
| Fake news and misinformation | Check facts with credible sources before sharing |
| Online predators and sextortion | Don’t chat privately with strangers; never share intimate images; report to the CSA (call/text 292) |
| Addiction and poor health | Set screen-time limits; keep phones out of the bedroom at night |
| Damage to reputation (digital footprint) | Think before you post; posts can affect future school admissions and jobs |
| Exposure to harmful content | Use age-appropriate platforms and content filters |

pages.title: Reply, Reply All and Forward
pages.body:
## Reply, Reply All and Forward
| **Button** | **Who receives it** | **When to use it** |
|---|---|---|
| Reply | Only the original **sender** | Your answer concerns only the sender |
| Reply All | The sender **and everyone** in the To and Cc fields (not Bcc) | Everyone needs to see your answer, e.g. a group project discussion |
| Forward | New people you choose; the original message and its **attachments** are included | Passing information to someone who was not on the original email |
| Forward several messages (“forward all”) | New recipients receive several emails together | Select several messages and choose **Forward** (Outlook) or **Forward as attachment** (Gmail) |
> 🛡️ **Safety first — Use Reply All carefully** A “Reply All” to hundreds of people (for example, a whole-school mailing list) can embarrass you and flood inboxes. Check the recipients before sending, and remove people who don’t need to see your reply.
> 💻 **Practical session**
Your teacher sends an email to the class with a Cc to the form master. (1) Reply only to the teacher with a question. (2) Reply All with your group’s progress update. (3) Forward the email with its attachment to a classmate who was absent, adding a short note.
